CNA description: prior to 2.5.301 and 3.1.7, InterfaceLookupFormatter<TKey,TElement> builds Dictionary<TKey,IGrouping<TKey,TElement>> with the default comparer instead of options.Security.GetEqualityComparer<TKey>(), enabling hash-collision CPU DoS on ILookup deserialization. CWE-407. Vendor GHSA-q2h6-ghwm-5qm8 is published (withdrawn_at null) and names API InterfaceLookupFormatter<TKey,TElement>.Create.

Source-to-sink at v3.1.6: CollectionFormatterBase.Deserialize (src/MessagePack/Formatters/CollectionFormatter.cs:430) reads the attacker-controlled array header (len = reader.ReadArrayHeader()), calls Create(len, options) (line 442), then Add() per element (line 449). InterfaceLookupFormatter.Create at v3.1.6:931 is return new Dictionary<TKey, IGrouping<TKey, TElement>>(count) (default comparer). Add at :921 is collection.Add(value.Key, value), so colliding attacker keys are the Dictionary insertion sink.

Sibling hash collections at the same tag already pass options.Security.GetEqualityComparer: HashSetFormatter.Create at v3.1.6 CollectionFormatter.cs:744 uses new HashSet<T>(options.Security.GetEqualityComparer<T>()); DictionaryFormatter.cs:156 uses new Dictionary<TKey,TValue>(count, options.Security.GetEqualityComparer<TKey>()). The lookup formatter is the omitted path. f6e167da1cb0f80182cb52a6135e25bc6cfc3cce (2020-01-03, 'Mitigate risk of hash collision attacks') introduced GetEqualityComparer on dictionary/hashset formatters and did not mention or patch InterfaceLookupFormatter.
